U.S. Commerce Secretary “South Korea agreed to fully open its market···$200 billion in investment for natural gas pipeline, AI, and more”

Published Oct 30, 2025 10:24 KST

  • By Yun Gi-Eun
Add to Google preferred sources

This article was translated by an AI tool. Feedback Here.

U.S. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick attends the Korea-U.S. Business Roundtable at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) CEO Summit held at Gyeongju Arts Center in Gyeongju on the 29th. Gyeongju | Lee Jun-heon

Howard Lutnick, the U.S. Commerce Secretary visiting South Korea, said that “South Korea agreed to open its domestic market.”

On the 30th, Lutnick wrote on X, “South Korea agreed to fully (100%) open its market.”

This differs from the South Korean government’s explanation that it blocked further opening of the agricultural market, including rice and beef.

Lutnick also said that of the $350 billion South Korea has agreed to invest in the United States (approximately 498 trillion won), $150 billion (approximately 213 trillion won) would be directed to shipbuilding. He added that President Trump would instruct that the remaining $200 billion (approximately 284 trillion won) be used for projects to be built in the United States. Specifically, he said the $200 billion would be invested in areas such as the Alaska natural gas pipeline, energy infrastructure, critical minerals, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence (AI), and quantum computing.

The United States, which finalized tariff talks with South Korea the previous day, decided to impose reciprocal tariffs of 15% on South Korea. Tariffs on automobiles and auto parts were reduced from 25% to 15%. However, Lutnick said that “tariffs on semiconductors are not included in this deal,” drawing a line.

The U.S. government has not yet set the tariff rate for South Korean semiconductor items. The South Korean government has said it agreed with the United States that, for semiconductors, the tariffs applied would not be disadvantageous compared with those on its main competitor, Taiwan. Lutnick’s remarks leave room for interpretation as an intention to renegotiate semiconductor tariffs with South Korea.

    뉴스레터 구독
    닫기

    뉴스레터를 구독해주셔서 감사합니다.

    전체 동의는 선택 항목에 대한 동의를 포함하고 있으며, 선택 항목에 대해 동의를 거부해도 서비스 이용이 가능합니다.

    보기

    개인정보 이용 목적- 뉴스레터 발송 및 CS처리, 공지 안내 등

    개인정보 수집 항목- 이메일 주소, 닉네임

    개인정보 보유 및 이용기간- 원칙적으로 개인정보 수집 및 이용목적이 달성된 후에 해당정보를 지체없이 파기합니다. 단, 관계법령의 규정에 의하여 보존할 필요가 있는 경우 일정기간 동안 개인정보를 보관할 수 있습니다.
    그 밖의 사항은 경향신문 개인정보취급방침을 준수합니다.

    보기

    경향신문의 새 서비스 소개, 프로모션 이벤트 등을 놓치지 않으시려면 '광고 동의'를 눌러 주세요.

    여러분의 관심으로 뉴스레터가 성장하면 뉴욕타임스, 월스트리트저널 등의 매체처럼 좋은 광고가 삽입될 수 있는데요. 이를 위한 '사전 동의'를 받는 것입니다. 많은 응원 부탁드립니다. (광고만 메일로 나가는 일은 '결코' 없습니다.)
